To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
management practices used to enhance crop production and quality have a net positive or negative impact on GHG emissions.
management practices used on cropllands can have a significant effect on net GWP and yieldscaled GWP.

the management practices used on cro-plands to enhance crop yield and quality can contribute 10–20 % of global GHGs and that net GWP and yieldscaled GWP can be used as a measure of the impact of agricultural practices on the global carbon cycle and as an indicator of the environmental sustainability of a cropping system.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following objectives: 1) to quantify the effects of various crop management practices on net GWP and yieldscaled GWP from croplands, 2) to develop novel management techniques to reduce the net GHGs from croplands.
the following: 1) quantification of GWP and GHGIs of different management practices used on croppands and 2) development of management strategies to minimize net CO 2 emission from croplands.
the impact of agricultural management on greenhouse gases and their effects on the global carbon cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
management practices that increase crop yield and quality will increase net GWP and net GHGI.
net GWP and net GHGI of a crop production system depends on the management practices and the crop species and variety used for crop production.

management techniques that increase the carbon sequestration rate in the soil and minimize the CO 2 emissions to the atmosphere would be the most desirable and effective way to reduce the net GHG emissions from cropland to the atmosphere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the management of agricultural systems has the potential to significantly mitigate net GWP from croplands.
the use of management practices that increase soil organic matter (SOM), such as no-till and cover cropping, can help to mitigate GHG emissions from agricultural lands.
management practices that enhance crop yield and quality also contribute to net CO 2 emission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
net CO 2 emission from croplands is a function of crop yields and management practices used.
management practices that enhance crop productivity and quality can be used to mitigate GHGs from the atmosphere.
net GWP is a better indicator of GHG emission than GHGI.
